title: Hot US October CPI lifts Fed hike bets; 2-year UST yield posts biggest jump since April 2025
content:
US CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month in October, above the 0.3% Reuters poll forecast, while core CPI rose 0.3% against expectations of 0.2%, according to the BLS. The BLS did not publish a 12-month rate because last year's government shutdown disrupted data collection. Fed Governor Christopher Waller backed a 25bp December hike and floated a 50bp move.

The 2-year UST yield jumped about 18bp to roughly **4.73%**, its largest one-day rise since the April 2025 tariff shock, and the 10-year briefly topped 5% before settling near **4.99%**. The S&P 500 fell **0.38%**, the DXY gained about 0.6% and gold dropped roughly 2%. Futures now fully price a 25bp hike at the 8–9 December FOMC, with a small chance of 50bp.

title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid spy-probe scandal; AI bellwether's slide deepens
content:
Nvidia said on 12 November that Jensen Huang had resigned as president, CEO and board member with immediate effect, ending a 33-year tenure. The move followed a board investigation, opened days earlier, into his relationship with a woman alleged to be a Chinese intelligence asset. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, Harvey Jones becomes the company's first board chair, and a search for a permanent CEO is under way.

Nvidia shares closed down **4.34%** on the day, CNBC reported, leaving the stock more than 20% lower over the past month. Reuters said the company had lost about **$600bn** in market value this week before the announcement. Chip weakness weighed on the Nasdaq, which fell **0.9%** on Friday even as the S&P 500 ended the week about 2.5% higher.

title: IEA sees first oil surplus since Iran war began as Gulf exports recover; Brent posts 2nd weekly fall
content:
The IEA said in its November Oil Market Report that the global market will return to surplus in Q4 for the first time since the Iran war began. It expects supply of about 105m bpd, 1.7m bpd above demand, reversing its earlier deficit forecast. Gulf exports excluding Oman recovered to 18.4m bpd in October, still 26% below pre-war levels, while the US blockade continues to curb Iranian flows. The agency sees a 2027 surplus of about 3.8m bpd.

Brent settled at **$95.84/bbl** on Friday and WTI at **$88.56/bbl**, with Brent down about **2.5%** on the week, its second straight weekly decline. Higher US crude inventories added pressure, although Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure and tanker attacks kept a geopolitical premium in prices.
